newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Float planned for Australia's Loy Yang A generator.
newsitem.headline: Float planned for Australia's Loy Yang A generator.

text.p: Australian institutions taking a 25 percent equity stake in Victoria state's Loy Yang A power station, to be privatised on Tuesday, aim to float some of their equity in about 12 months, a source said.

Horizon Energy Investments Ltd, comprising Macquarie Bank's Infrastructure Trust of Australia Group Ltd and other local institutions, is part of a consortium led by U.S. utilities CMS Energy Corp and NRG Energy Inc.
The consortium's bid of A$4.75 billion is said to have been accepted by the Victoria state government, which put the 2,000 megawatt station and associated coal mine up for sale.
An announcement is expected around 0200 GMT (midday). The government has so far declined to comment on the bidding.
The government has insisted the power station not be floated onto the Australian Stock Exchange for at least 12 months after it is sold.
"Horizon cannot be floated for 12 months, but it's fair to say it (the float) will be shortly after," a source close to the bidding told Reuters.
Horizon owns about 25 percent of the consortium, with CMS owning about 50 percent and NRG the remaining 25 percent.
Infrastructure Trust, which was floated by Macquarie Bank late last year, sought a trading halt on its stock on Monday pending the Loy Yang announcement.
